predecessors.name: Western Roman Empire
predecessors.text: Gallaecia, the Roman province of north-western Hispania: the Suevi 'moved to Galicia between 409 and 411' and in 411 took the west of it by lot, the Hasding Vandals the east (Kingdom of the Suebi and…

successors.name: Visigothic Kingdom
successors.text: Gallaecia, which Leovigild conquered in 585 ('In 585, Liuvigild conquered the Suebi peoples, bringing an end to some forty-years of their independence in Spain', Leovigild page)

ledger.x: 411: the Suevi get the west of Gallaecia by lot.
419: the Suevi drive the Vandals out of Gallaecia.

427: Heremigarius, the Suevi's leader in Lusitania (427-429), is the only hint of Suebi land south of the Mondego before 439; in 429 he plundered Lusitania until, confronted by Gaiseric, he drowned in the Guadiana.
439: the court moves to Mérida; the move back to Braga is not dated by the pages opened.

441: Rechila takes Seville. he took the capital 'Seville in 441'; 'The provinces of Lusitania, Baetica, and Carthaginiensis were subjected to the Suevi' except the Levante and the Mediterranean seaboard.
456: the Visigoths of Theodoric II break the Suebi at the Órbigo.
456: the Gothic campaign in Gallaecia ends with Rechiar's capture at Porto and his execution in December.
460: Richimund takes Lugo and makes it his seat.
569: Leovigild opens the Visigothic reconquest of the Suebian marches.

wars.name: Suebi-Vandal war of 419
wars.outcome: Roman general Asterius intervened and forced the Hasding Vandals to leave Gallaecia for Baetica; Hermeric, trapped in the Narbasian (Erbasian) mountains, was relieved and the whole of Gallaecia passed to the Suevi.

wars.name: Suebian raids on Gallaecia
wars.outcome: Hermeric began raiding in 430; Hydatius sought Aetius's help in 431, Censorius was sent in 432; peace on episcopal intervention in 435 (bishop Symphosius).

wars.name: Suebian conquest of Lusitania and Baetica
wars.outcome: Rechila defeated Andevotus on the Genil in 438, took Mérida in 439, Mértola in 440 and Seville in 441; Lusitania, Baetica and Carthaginensis 'were subjected to the Suevi' except the Levante.

wars.name: Visigothic campaign of 456 (Battle of the Órbigo)
wars.outcome: Theodoric II defeated Rechiar on 5 October 456, took Braga (28 October), Rechiar was captured at Porto and executed in December; in July 458 a Gothic army reached Baetica and the Suebi lost the south.

wars.name: Majorian's operation against the Suebi
wars.outcome: The page says only that Majorian's campaign 'started with an operation against the Suebi in North-Western Hispania, lasting the whole of 459'; under the treaty of 458 the Visigoths 'had to relinquish their vast conquests in Hispania'.

wars.name: Visigothic wars against the Suebi
wars.outcome: Leovigild's first campaign (569) subdued Zamora, Palencia and León; Miro accepted a tributary treaty in 576; Leovigild conquered the Suebi in 585 and annexed Gallaecia.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes any Suebian frontier: the pages name cities and provinces (Braga, Mérida, Seville, Lisbon, Zamora, León), not lines.
